correctness.rationale: After symplectic normalization, integer symplectic area places the two core lattice vectors in the integer lattice with determinant magnitude equal to the positive integer area. The rational-rank-two hypothesis permits an integer unimodular coordinate change that sends the fourth point to one irrational and one rational coordinate while keeping the core vectors integral. In the critical-source Zak-transform proof, the only step that uses unimodularity of the two core characters is the claim that the lattice trinomial has finitely many torus zeros. For determinant magnitude q, the corresponding character homomorphism of the two-torus is a surjective degree-q covering. The target trinomial has at most two torus zeros, so its pullback has at most two-q zeros and remains finite. The complete critical-source proof was inspected through the normal form, exact return multiplier, finite-zero lemma, zero-free active arc, winding obstruction, holonomy and final Laurent contradiction. Those later steps require integrality, irrational return and finite exceptional set, all preserved by the degree-q replacement. Thus the source argument extends to every positive integer area without relying on finite numerical evidence.

originality.rationale: The complete current critical mixed-arithmetic proof was materially read. It proves the rational-rank-two case at critical area one and explicitly isolates the finite zero set of a unimodular lattice trinomial before the winding/holonomy part of the proof. Its covolume/rational-rank status discussion marks the supercritical rank-two cell as only partially classified. The earlier large-covolume theorem covers the maximally rationally independent rank-three case and separate rational-coordinate cases, not rational rank two. The submitted finite-index covering lemma therefore fills a natural infinite arithmetic subfamily of an explicitly incomplete supercritical cell. Targeted Resultary and literature searches did not locate an earlier all-positive-integer-covolume rank-two theorem.
residual_risks: A very recent post-status-table paper could conceivably solve a broader supercritical rational-rank-two class under different terminology; targeted current searches did not locate one.

value.rationale: The theorem advances an explicitly partially classified HRT parameter cell by an infinite arithmetic family, extending the critical area-one result to every positive integer area for rational rank two. The finite-index torus-covering replacement is a structural lemma that preserves the entire later holonomy mechanism and is plausibly reusable in further lattice-index extensions. This is a motivated boundary/generalization rather than an arbitrary parameter sample.

limitations: The theorem covers positive integer symplectic area only.
It does not classify noninteger supercritical rational-rank-two configurations or the entire remaining supercritical mixed-arithmetic cell.
No claim is made about subcritical counterexample regimes.
